recipes.name: Seven Layer Tortilla Pie
ingredients_raw: 2 (15 ounce) cans pinto beans, drained and rinsed
1 (15 ounce) can black beans, rinsed and drained

steps.text: Preheat oven to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C).
In a large bowl, mash pinto beans. Stir in 3/4 cup salsa and garlic.
In a separate bowl, mix together 1/4 cup salsa, cilantro, black beans and tomatoes.

Place 1 tortilla in a pie plate or tart dish. Spread 3/4 cup pinto bean mixture over tortilla to within 1/2 inch of edge. Top with 1/4 cup cheese, and cover with another tortilla. Spread with 2/3 cup black bean mixture, and top with 1/4 cup cheese. Repeat layering twice. Cover with remaining tortilla, and spread with remaining pinto bean mixture and cheese.
Cover with foil, and bake in preheated oven for about 40 minutes. Cut into wedges, and serve with salsa and sour cream.

raw_recipe.headline: Seven Layer Tortilla Pie
raw_recipe.description: Southwest cooking at its best. Two different kinds of beans are zipped up with picante sauce, cilantro, garlic and tomato, and then layered between a stack of flour tortillas. Pop into a hot oven and 40 minutes later it emerges - seven layers of delight.

review.reviewBody: This was super easy and fun to make! I added green chiles, black olives, corn, and shredded up some rotisserie chicken and layered it on as I saw fit, topping each layer with cheese. I also used low fat refried beans, low fat black beans, and low fat mexican cheese to make it that much more healthy! After it came out of the oven, I put some sliced avocado and tomatoes on, and it was a hit! My boyfriend couldn't get enough (in fact writing this review makes me want to whip one up right now!!!) Give it a try tonight!

This was awesome! I have a suggestion for improving texture and flavor. Toast each side of the tortillas in a very lightly oiled skillet before layering. This adds a roasty flavor and makes them more resistant to sogginess. I used 1 can of rotel instead of salsa+tomatoes, and added a layer of cooked chicken seasoned with chili powder. I used a springform pan somewhat larger than the burrito-sized tortillas and that gave great crunch as the hot oven air could crisp the edges. Next time I will add some raw chopped onion in the pinto layer. Also, as suggested, I lightly oiled the springform pan so there was no sticking–and there wasn't, but for easier cleanup, I will line the bottom with parchment. The coolest thing about this recipe is that nothing needs sauteeing as it's written. It's really easy and rotation-worthy.

Delicious & relatively easy to make. I ended with 3 tortillas on top and thought that seemed like a lot, but it turned out great! I added 1/2 can white corn to the black bean mix and I also seasoned the mix with hot chili powder, cumin & garlic powder to give it that taco taste. Oh also, I didn’t have fresh cilantro on hand so I used dried cilantro and didn’t notice any problem. I added medium enchilada sauce (on top of the last bean mix, before the last of the cheese) & sliced black olives on top before putting in the oven for 40 minutes @400 degrees in my 9x9 ceramic casserole dish. Served with sour cream & Franks hot sauce. Came out hot & a little crispy. It sliced with a spatula easier than I thought it would AND it stayed in a wedge to the plate!

I made this easy casserole for our dinner last night. I really like that this recipe is quite versatile in what you can do with it. I replaced the two cans of pinto beans with one can of fat free refried beans. I used low sodium black beans, and canned diced tomatoes with green chilies, instead of fresh tomatoes. The cheese I used was Monterey jack. I added half a taco seasoning packet to each bean mixture, but I'm not sure it was needed. We topped this with sour cream, and salsa or taco sauce. I sliced this into eight servings, instead of 6, and that smaller serving was plenty. It worked beautifully in my covered, glass, round casserole dish. The kids really liked this, and we had no leftovers. This will become a regular in our house. This could easily be made with corn tortillas. I may make this when my son's friend, who has a wheat allergy, stays with us. He also has a dairy allergy, but the cheese could easily be left off. Then it could be placed on the table with other condiments for people to add as they wish. In the future, I think I will replace both the salsa and tomatoes with pico de gallo. I served this with a green salad, and it made the perfect Sunday night meal. It could easily be made ahead, ready to pop in the oven on busy weeknights. Olives, chicken, corn, avocados, and ground beef could be used to change it up.

Very good recipe and fun to make. Took other reviewer's suggestions and added shredded chicken (with Mexican seasonings), corn, green chilies, and used refried beans instead of mashing up pintos, and drizzled enchilada sauce over the chicken layers. Used Monterrey Jack as the cheese. I toasted the flour tortillas way too much, next time I'm going to check on them earlier, but it was fine. My boyfriend was thinking it wasn't going to be this good and he was amazed by the results and can't wait to have it again. I used a springform pan to bake it in.

I followed some of the other reviews and used chicken, jalapeños, and tomato sauce. I boiled some chicken quarters and added some oregano, cumin, bay leaf, garlic powder, onion powder, Goya, and crushed red pepper. 
One of the other reviewers used enchilada sauce, I took the recommendation and made by own with the canned tomato sauce, some of the chicken broth, Goya, and mixed it with the shredded chicken. 
I layered the tortillas with black beans, pepper jack cheese, sharp cheddar cheese, shredded chicken, jalapeños, salsa, a small amount of brown rice, and seasoned tomato sauce. I had enough chicken broth to freeze and use for another recipe. Thanks KDCG!

We really liked this one and it was nice to have something different. I only had dried beans so had to plan ahead and soak and cook them. I used half the amount of pinto beans called for and added a pound of ground beef sautéed with chili powder, salt, cumin, oregano and cayenne. I also found the black bean mixture bland so added salt to taste and about a 1/4 cup more of salsa. I omitted the cilantro due to the fact that DH hates it but it would have gone well in my opinion. Great recipe that is very versatile based on what you have!

My changes were, I baked the tortillas some, used 1 can of refried beans in place of one of the cans of pinto beans, added fresh diced jalapenos, a can of diced green chilis drained, used mexican blend cheese, also added black olives to each layer and topped it with enchilada sauce. It turned out great!

I made this for company last night. It was delicious. After reading many of the other reviews I incorporated the most frequent suggestions (fewer layers, refried beans, adding ground beef seasoned with taco seasoning, making it in a spring form pan). I ended up with 4 layers only (2 each of the bean tomato layer and the ground beef, onion, olive, layer with cheese on each) ending with beef and then cheese. Baked covered for 40 minutes and then uncovered for 10-15 minutes. It was a big hit. I'll make it again.

We tailored this recipe to our tastes. We added chopped red onion, fresh jalapeno, way more cilantro, 4 cloves garlic instead of 2, and less salsa in both of the bean mixes to prevent getting soggy like I've seen in other comments.
We only had one can of pinto beans, so ours ended up making about 4 layers instead of 7. We will make it again!

This is tasty. We added 1/2 lb of chorizo into one of the black bean layers and added black olives to the top. Next time I will bake a little longer so the middle is warmer. Going to freeze some and see how it does.

I have made this before and thought it was a bit to soggy for our liking. The taste is good for a vegetarian dish, so i decided to try it again, this time subbing tostadas for tortillas(Mentioned by previous reviewer). This made a HUGE difference. Although a bit more tricky to put together with the tostadas, i will never go back.

I've been making this recipe for several years and served not only to family but also to dinner guests...Every person who has eaten it RAVES about not only for its flavors but also the ease with which it is prepared! Will continue making it for all years ahead!! Each tim÷ I've prepared it I've added two cups of rotisserie chicken & a can of drained Nibley corn...Excellent!!

I love this recipe! I added corn to the black bean layers, and used Sun-dried tomato tortillas. I have the genetic mutation that makes cilantro taste like soap, and it's delicious without it. It also reheats really well, and makes for excellent leftovers.
Even after toasting the tortillas beforehand, all the layers but the top turned mushy. Wet dough. I would try this again and use tostadas instead. It needs a crunchy element. Good recipe!
Everyone loved it! Used corn tortillas instead, and doubled the cilantro as per other reviewers. Topped it with avocado and pico de gallo. Yum!

It was very easy to make. I changed it by replacing chicken chili sauce for the beans. I added the cheese, I also served onions & green peppers on the side, with black olives and the sour cream. Delish! You could use just about anything as the fillings. A very flexable recipe.
